answer: Bonded trust graphs resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to hold a minimum max-flow capacity from trusted roots over edges backed by slashable collateral. Because every active node consumes bounded endorsement capacity along cut edges, an attacker must lock liquid capital or burn real peer trust per fake identity for tasks spanning meadow surveys, velvet looms, or nebula spectra. However, wealthy adversaries can still bypass edge scarcity through off-band bribes to endorsers.
